rows.answer: About 4 bp lower at the same FICO and about 5 bp higher at the same score number (VS4 720 against FICO 720), so where both scores show, its rate has averaged between the rates of FICO loans at those two scores. Same FICO: zero is not ruled out, and the figure runs about −2 to −5 depending on what is held equal. Rocket retail, about half these loans, carries most of it, and there it grows, as the LLPA gap does, with how far VS4 sits above FICO: about −4.5 at 20 to 39 above and about −11 at 40+. Same LLPA: about 0 overall, which does not show the LLPA caused the gap. About 45% of these loans are FICO 780+, where rates stop falling with the score; below 780 it is about −4, with the methods running −6 to +2. About 5 bp higher at the same score number under 820, at every lender group shown. 95% range about +4 to +6.5. It says a VS4 number has got the rate of a lower FICO, not that VS4 costs more.
rows.changed: Replaces the rate figures shown here before Oct 31, which blended two comparisons, and restates the dated figures of Oct 31 with Rocket correspondent out of every all-lender row, the LLPA tier split under 640 and the 95% range on the estimate.
rows.equivalent_caption: VS4 loans at Rocket and UWM sit well above FICO: a VS4 of 720-739 goes with a FICO near 690 there and near 732 at lenders that rarely use VS4. This is how these lenders have priced, not a conversion.
rows.equivalent_more: Which FICO pays the same (95% ranges, which resample weeks, not lenders, so they run narrow): about 15 to 27 at Rocket retail, about 14 to 32 at UWM. A 1 bp change in the gap moves this about 4.5 points.
rows.equivalent_stat: On average, a FICO about 19 to 30 points below the VS4 number (95% range). Near the old rule's 20 points, which does not show the rule caused it.
rows.expected: How much to expect: below FICO 780, full credit for the VS4 number (priced like the same FICO number) would be about −4, against −6 to +2 across the methods, so this row cannot tell full credit from none.
rows.gap_line: At Rocket retail, the further VS4 sits above FICO, the lower the rate at the same FICO; elsewhere that shows only on the model. At the same score number it is highest at 40+ above.
rows.lender_line: UWM: its same-FICO gap moves with the comparison: about −1 on its VS4 loans showing a FICO, about −3 on VS4 under 820, and about +2 against FICO loans that also show a VS4.
rows.lender_rates: On rate, at the same FICO: Rocket retail about −7.5 bp, other groups about −1 to 0, on few weeks of loans. Refinances are 68% of Rocket retail's loans here and 22% of the others', but the methods disagree on whether its gap is wider on refinances.
rows.llpa_share: VS4's LLPA is lower on about 28% of all loans showing both scores, whichever score priced them.
rows.llpa_sum: Where VS4 lowers the LLPA, the LLPA is about 56.5 bp of balance lower on today's grid, about 11.5 bp of rate at the rule of thumb of 5 bp of LLPA to 1 bp of rate; on the old rule in force when most of these rates were likely set, about 34 bp, about 7 bp of rate. The rate itself differs by about −8.5 to −5.5 bp. The files cannot tell where any difference goes: points, lender credits or the lender's margin. By lender it is not even: Rocket retail −12.5 to −9.5 against an old-rule LLPA gap worth about 7.5 bp of rate, UWM broker −6 to 0 against about 6.5.
rows.milliman_line: Not the same comparison: Milliman takes 20 points off VS4 first and holds the LLPA. On that basis, with channel and finer score bands held, about +3.5 on loans closed and issued May to August, its window (about +1.5 on those first disclosed from Jul 20, where the other figures here start), and about +1 on Rocket and UWM loans issued from Oct 1. Without channel, with VS4 820+ and Rocket correspondent kept, about +6.5 in its window; any gap left to its figure is not explained here.

rows.number_blend: VS4 640-819 is about 90% of the +5's loans: about +7.5 where the old rule would raise the LLPA and about +1 on the rest (mostly VS4 780-819 or LTV 60 or under).

rows.sample: The sample holds 29,005 VS4 and 461,623 FICO loans, Rocket correspondent left out.
rows.stamp: VS4 loans (those priced on VS4, Rocket correspondent left out) are compared with FICO loans of the same lender, channel, week first disclosed, closing month, GSE, purpose, LTV range and score (within 5 points or one LLPA tier), where a match exists, on 30-year fixed loans.
rows.stamp_more: Three methods: exact match with a 5-point score band; exact match with one LLPA tier as the band (20 points under 640); and a model fitted on FICO loans, by lender and channel where possible, that also controls for occupancy, units, property type, second liens, loan size, DTI, mortgage insurance, state, first-time buyers, number of borrowers and loan program. The dot is the midpoint of the first two and the bar the range across all three. Closing month is estimated from the first payment date. The grid matches Fannie Mae's matrix of Sep 30, 2026.
rows.test_line: A test: FICO loans with VS4 20+ above their FICO should show about 0 if a high VS4 lowers the rate only when it is the score picked. They show about +1 at lenders that rarely use VS4 and about −7 at UWM on 189 loans (about −11 on its 116 correspondent loans, about 0 on its 73 broker loans): thin evidence that a high VS4 goes with a lower rate there even on FICO loans. Rocket has too few such loans to test (10).

rows.text: About 4 bp lower at the same FICO and about 5 bp higher at the same score number (VS4 720 against FICO 720), so where both scores show, its rate has averaged between the rates of FICO loans at those two scores.

Same FICO: zero is not ruled out, and the figure runs about −2 to −5 depending on what is held equal. Rocket retail, about half these loans, carries most of it, and there it grows, as the LLPA gap does, with how far VS4 sits above FICO: about −4.5 at 20 to 39 above and about −11 at 40+.

Same LLPA: about 0 overall, which does not show the LLPA caused the gap. About 45% of these loans are FICO 780+, where rates stop falling with the score; below 780 it is about −4, with the methods running −6 to +2.
About 5 bp higher at the same score number under 820, at every lender group shown. 95% range about +4 to +6.5. It says a VS4 number has got the rate of a lower FICO, not that VS4 costs more.
Fee or score? These files cannot settle it: lenders can pick the score, sometimes after the rate is set, and lock dates do not show. So this shows where a gap sits, not what choosing VS4 is worth.
Note rate only: discount points, lender credits and lock dates are not disclosed. −4 bp is about 0.2 of a discount point.
Narrow base: Rocket and UWM are 97% of these VS4 loans. Same-FICO loans are about 79% of VS4 loans issued since Oct 1, as no earlier loan shows both scores.
VS4 loans under 820 that show a FICO, about one in four: about +5 at the same number and about −5.5 at the same FICO (95% range about −7.5 to −0.5).

At Rocket's switch point (20 points above FICO): where the LLPA would not change, the rate moves about +3 (95% range about −8.5 to +14, on few weeks of loans). The same test at about 90 other cut-offs where nothing switches swings about −11 to +11, so it cannot see a step under about 10 bp.

Past the switch point: at Rocket, VS4 25 to 49 points above FICO is about −11 to −2.5, on few weeks of loans, against FICO loans with the same FICO and VS4 0 to 19 points above it, where the LLPA is the same today and under the old rule. At UWM that comparison is about 0 to +12.5 on two methods. Rocket's choice of score and its higher VS4 come together, so this cannot say which.
A range in bp with no label is the spread across the 3 methods, not a margin of error.
Left out of same FICO: VS4 loans showing no FICO (unknown, not counted as having none). Left out of every all-lender rate row: Rocket correspondent, not like for like.
Which grid: lower and same LLPA are sorted on the one grid in force since Oct 1; most of these rates were likely set earlier, under the old rule that counted VS4 20 points lower.

Controls, same FICO: about −3 with only lender, channel, week, GSE and FICO; about −2 in a simple regression; about −5 on exact match within 5 points; about −3 on exact match within one LLPA tier; about −3.5 on the model, which also holds occupancy, units, property type, second liens, loan size, DTI, mortgage insurance, state, first-time buyers, number of borrowers and loan program.

The thin line: it resamples about 15 lender and channel groups, about 3 carrying most of the weight, so treat it as the minimum uncertainty. With Rocket correspondent back, the lower-LLPA range reaches +2.
Which loans match: by exact match, 3,500 to 5,300 of about 7,400 same-FICO loans and 13,100 to 19,100 of about 22,700 same-number loans find FICO loans to compare.
Over time: Rocket retail's gap looks smaller on later loans, on few weeks of loans: about −12 to −5 closed in September and −5.5 to −3 closed in October. All others: about −3 to +0.5.
The newest file is provisional.

rows.text: At the same FICO, lender, channel, timing, purpose and LTV range, VS4 loans issued from Oct 1 and showing a FICO ran about 4 bp below FICO loans' note rates (95% range about −7 to +0.5), before points and lender credits, which do not show. Most of it is Rocket retail, about −7.5 against about −1 to 0 at other lender groups (−8.5 to −4.5 and −4 to +1.5 across the methods), on few weeks of loans. Refinances are 68% of Rocket retail's loans here and 22% of the others', but the methods disagree on whether its gap is wider on refinances. Most of these rates were likely set before the Sep 29 announcement of one LLPA grid for both scores. Across lenders the gap is about −7 where VS4 has the lower LLPA on the Oct 1 grid and about level where the LLPA is the same (about −4 below FICO 780, where all the lower-LLPA loans sit; −6 to +2 across the methods), which does not show the LLPA caused it. Lenders can pick the score, so this shows where a gap sits, not what choosing VS4 is worth. Rocket correspondent is left out; with it the top of the range is +4.5.

At the same FICO, where both scores carry the same LLPA on the Oct 1 grid, VS4 loans issued from Oct 1 ran about level with FICO loans' note rates (95% range about −3 to +5): about +2 bp at FICO 780+, where rates stop falling with the score, and about −4 bp below 780 (−6 to +2 across the methods), so this cannot tell a discount there from none. Most of these rates were likely set earlier, when the LLPA grid counted VS4 as 20 points lower. Rocket correspondent is left out; with it the top of the range is +8.

At the same score number under 820 (VS4 720 against FICO 720), VS4 loans first disclosed from Jul 20 ran about 5 bp above FICO loans' note rates (95% range about +4 to +6.5), higher at every lender group large enough to read, with Rocket correspondent left out. That says a VS4 number has got the rate of a lower FICO, not that VS4 costs more: where a FICO shows (loans issued from Oct 1, about one of these in four), they are about 5.5 bp below the rate at their FICO (95% range about −7.5 to −0.5 under 820; with 820+ it reaches +0.5). About one VS4 loan in five is 820+ and not in this figure. The 5 bp is about $12 a month on $350,000, before points and lender credits, which do not show.

On average a VS4 number under 820 has got the rate of a FICO about 19 to 30 points lower (95% range, too narrow: it resamples weeks, not lenders), on loans issued from Oct 1, most with rates likely set while the LLPA grid still counted VS4 as 20 points lower. That is near those 20 points, which does not show the grid caused it. This is how Rocket and UWM have priced, Rocket correspondent left out, not a conversion.
